courses.title: Management Concepts and Organisational Behaviour, MCom Semester 1
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (BU MCom CBCS, 2024-25)

topics.title: Approaches to management
topics.summary: Classical, behavioural, quantitative, systems and contingency approaches.
notes: Classical: scientific management (Taylor), administrative (Fayol), bureaucratic (Weber).
Behavioural: human relations (Mayo), Maslow, McGregor.
Systems and contingency approaches treat management as situational and open to the environment.
outcomes: Apply a contingency view to a case

topics.title: Perception, personality and learning
topics.summary: Individual determinants of behaviour at work.
notes: Perceptual shortcuts: halo effect, stereotyping, contrast effect, projection.
Personality: Big Five; locus of control (internal vs external).
Reinforcement schedules: continuous, fixed/variable interval, fixed/variable ratio.

topics.title: Motivation and leadership theories
topics.summary: Content and process theories and leadership models.
notes: Herzberg, McClelland, Vroom (M = E × I × V), Adams (equity), Locke (goal setting).
Leadership: trait, behavioural, situational (Hersey–Blanchard), path–goal, transformational.
Emotional intelligence (Goleman): self-awareness, self-regulation, motivation, empathy, social skill.

topics.title: Groups, conflict and change
topics.summary: Teams, conflict and organisational change and development.
notes: Group cohesiveness raises productivity when group norms support organisational goals.
Conflict can be functional or dysfunctional.
Organisational development interventions: sensitivity training, survey feedback, team building.

courses.title: Managerial Economics, MCom Semester 1
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (BU MCom CBCS, 2024-25)

topics.title: Demand analysis and forecasting
topics.summary: Elasticities, demand estimation and forecasting.
notes: Point elasticity e = (dQ/dP)(P/Q).
Demand estimation by regression: Q = a + bP + cY + …
Forecasting: survey methods, trend projection, barometric indicators, econometric models.
outcomes: Forecast demand with a trend equation

topics.title: Production and cost analysis
topics.summary: Isoquants, economies of scope and break-even analysis.
notes: An isoquant shows input combinations giving the same output; MRTS = MPL ÷ MPK.
Economies of scope: cheaper to produce products together than separately.
Learning curve: unit cost falls by a constant percentage each time cumulative output doubles.

topics.title: Pricing strategies and market structures
topics.summary: Pricing under competition and monopoly, and pricing practices.
notes: Monopoly mark-up: (P − MC) ÷ P = −1 ÷ e (Lerner index).
Third-degree price discrimination charges more in the market with less elastic demand.
Game theory: Nash equilibrium is a set of strategies where no player gains by changing alone.

topics.title: Macroeconomic policy and business
topics.summary: Monetary and fiscal policy, inflation and business cycles.
notes: Inflation types: demand-pull, cost-push; Phillips curve trade-off in the short run.
RBI's monetary policy committee sets the repo rate to target 4% CPI inflation within a 2–6% band.
Fiscal deficit = Total expenditure − (Revenue receipts + non-debt capital receipts).

courses.title: Advanced Cost and Management Accounting, MCom Semester 1
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (BU MCom CBCS, 2024-25)

topics.title: ABC system
topics.summary: Activities, cost drivers and ABC vs traditional costing.
notes: ABC assigns overheads to activities, then to products by cost drivers (set-ups, orders, inspections).
Activity cost driver rate = Activity cost pool ÷ Cost driver volume.
ABC corrects cross-subsidisation where low-volume products are under-costed.
outcomes: Compare ABC with traditional absorption costing

lesson.hook: A factory makes 10,000 standard shirts and 100 custom ones. Why might the custom shirts look profitable but not be?
lesson.example:
Set-up cost ₹60,000 for 30 set-ups: ₹2,000 per set-up. Custom line uses 20 set-ups = ₹40,000 for 100 shirts: ₹400 each.
Spread by labour hours instead, the custom shirts might get only ₹20 each of set-up cost.

questions.a: A factor whose change causes a change in the cost of an activity.

topics.title: Target, life cycle and kaizen costing
topics.summary: Modern costing techniques for strategy.
notes: Target cost = Target price − Target profit.
Life cycle costing covers costs from design to disposal.
Kaizen costing seeks continuous small cost reductions during production.
outcomes: Compute target cost and cost gap

topics.title: Relevant costing
topics.summary: Relevant costs, make or buy, special orders and limiting factors.
notes: Relevant costs are future, incremental cash costs; sunk costs are irrelevant.
Opportunity cost is relevant when resources are scarce.
With one limiting factor, rank products by contribution per unit of that factor.
outcomes: Make make-or-buy and special order decisions

topics.title: Responsibility accounting and transfer pricing
topics.summary: Responsibility centres, ROI, residual income and transfer pricing.
notes: Centres: cost, revenue, profit and investment centres.
ROI = Operating profit ÷ Capital employed; residual income = Profit − (Capital × Cost of capital).
Transfer price range: minimum = marginal cost + opportunity cost; maximum = external market price.
outcomes: Evaluate divisions by ROI and RI

courses.title: Corporate Financial Reporting, MCom Semester 2
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (BU MCom CBCS, 2024-25)

topics.title: Ind AS and IFRS
topics.summary: Conceptual framework and key Ind AS.
notes: Ind AS 1 presentation; Ind AS 8 accounting policies, estimates and errors; Ind AS 10 events after the reporting period.
Ind AS 115 revenue: five steps — identify contract, performance obligations, transaction price, allocate, recognise.
Ind AS 116 leases: lessees recognise right-of-use assets and lease liabilities for most leases.
outcomes: Account for a lease under Ind AS 116

topics.title: Ind AS 103 and consolidation
topics.summary: Acquisition method, goodwill and consolidated statements.
notes: Acquisition method: identify acquirer, acquisition date, measure assets and liabilities at fair value, recognise goodwill or bargain purchase.
Goodwill = Consideration + NCI + previously held interest − Net identifiable assets.
Ind AS 110: control means power, exposure to variable returns and ability to use power to affect returns.
outcomes: Prepare a simple consolidated balance sheet

topics.title: Ind AS 109 and 32
topics.summary: Classification, measurement and impairment of financial instruments.
notes: Financial assets: amortised cost, FVOCI or FVTPL depending on business model and cash flow characteristics.
Expected credit loss model for impairment.
Compound instruments (convertible debentures) are split into liability and equity components.

topics.title: Integrated and sustainability reporting
topics.summary: Non-financial reporting frameworks.
notes: BRSR is mandatory for the top 1,000 listed companies; BRSR Core needs reasonable assurance for the top companies in phases.
Integrated reporting (IIRC) covers six capitals.
ISSB standards (IFRS S1, S2) set global sustainability disclosure baselines.

courses.title: Business Research Methods, MCom Semester 2
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (BU MCom CBCS, 2024-25)

topics.title: Research problem and design
topics.summary: Problem formulation, hypotheses and designs.
notes: Research questions should be specific and answerable.
Designs: exploratory, descriptive, causal.
Variables: independent, dependent, moderating, mediating.

topics.title: Sampling and scales
topics.summary: Sampling techniques, sample size and measurement validity.
notes: n = z²σ² ÷ e² for estimating a mean.
Validity types: content, construct, criterion; reliability: test–retest, internal consistency.
Scales: Likert, semantic differential, rank order.

topics.title: Parametric and non-parametric tests
topics.summary: t, F, chi-square and non-parametric tests.
notes: Paired t-test compares before–after means.
Chi-square test of independence: χ² = Σ (O − E)² ÷ E with (r − 1)(c − 1) df.
Non-parametric: sign test, Wilcoxon, Mann–Whitney, Kruskal–Wallis.
outcomes: Choose and run a suitable test

lesson.example: Observed 30 and 20 against expected 25 and 25: χ² = 25/25 + 25/25 = 2; with 1 df, below 3.84, so not significant at 5%.

topics.title: Research report
topics.summary: Writing, presenting and referencing research.
notes: Structure: introduction, review, methodology, analysis, findings, conclusions.
Tables and figures need numbers, titles and sources.
Cite with a consistent style (APA).

courses.title: International Business, MCom Semester 2
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (BU MCom CBCS, 2024-25)

topics.title: Globalisation and trade theories
topics.summary: Globalisation, trade theories and protectionism.
notes: Comparative advantage and Heckscher–Ohlin factor endowment theory.
Tariff and non-tariff barriers (quotas, standards, anti-dumping duties).
Product life cycle theory of trade (Vernon).

topics.title: FDI and multinational enterprises
topics.summary: Types and theories of FDI and India's FDI policy.
notes: FDI types: horizontal, vertical, conglomerate; greenfield vs brownfield.
Dunning's OLI paradigm: ownership, location, internalisation advantages.
India's FDI is through the automatic route or the government route depending on sector caps.

topics.title: Exchange rates and risk
topics.summary: Exchange rate determination and exposure management.
notes: Purchasing power parity: exchange rate changes offset inflation differentials.
Interest rate parity: F = S × (1 + i_d) ÷ (1 + i_f).
Hedging: forwards, futures, options and natural hedges.
outcomes: Compute forward rates by interest rate parity

topics.title: India's trade policy and the WTO
topics.summary: Foreign Trade Policy, export promotion and WTO agreements.
notes: Foreign Trade Policy 2023 aims at export growth and ease of doing business; DGFT administers it.
Export promotion: SEZs, EOUs, export credit (ECGC, EXIM Bank).
WTO agreements: GATT, GATS, TRIPS, TRIMs.

courses.title: Direct Taxes and Tax Planning, MCom Semester 3
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (BU MCom CBCS, 2025-26)

topics.title: Tax planning, avoidance and evasion
topics.summary: Distinguishing planning, avoidance and evasion, and GAAR.
notes: Tax planning uses provisions as intended; avoidance exploits loopholes; evasion is illegal.
GAAR (Chapter X-A) lets authorities deny benefits of impermissible avoidance arrangements.
McDowell and Vodafone judgments shaped the Indian position on avoidance.

topics.title: Taxation of companies
topics.summary: Corporate tax rates, MAT and concessional regimes.
notes: Section 115BAA: 22% (effective about 25.17%) for domestic companies forgoing certain deductions; MAT does not apply.
Section 115BAB (new manufacturing companies) 15% for companies set up before its sunset date.
MAT (section 115JB) at 15% of book profit for companies under the normal regime.

topics.title: Tax-based managerial decisions
topics.summary: Make or buy, lease or buy, and capital structure.
notes: Interest is tax-deductible; dividends are not, so debt gives a tax shield (Interest × tax rate).
Lease or buy: compare after-tax present values of costs.
Depreciation tax shield = Depreciation × tax rate.
outcomes: Compare lease and buy after tax

topics.title: Returns, assessment and appeals
topics.summary: Filing returns, assessment types and appeals.
notes: Assessment types: summary (143(1)), scrutiny (143(3)), best judgement (144), reassessment (147–148A).
Faceless assessment and appeals schemes.
Appeals: CIT(A), ITAT, High Court, Supreme Court.

courses.title: Advanced Financial Management (Finance elective), MCom Semester 3
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (BU MCom CBCS, 2025-26)

topics.title: Corporate valuation
topics.summary: DCF, relative valuation and EVA.
notes: Free cash flow to firm = EBIT(1 − t) + Depreciation − Capex − ΔWorking capital.
Firm value = PV of FCFF at WACC + terminal value (FCFF × (1 + g) ÷ (WACC − g)).
EVA = NOPAT − WACC × Capital employed.

topics.title: M&A analysis
topics.summary: Synergy, exchange ratios and takeover regulation.
notes: Synergy = V(AB) − (V(A) + V(B)).
Exchange ratio based on EPS, market price or book value.
SEBI SAST Regulations: open offer triggered at 25% voting rights.

topics.title: Derivatives for corporate risk
topics.summary: Using futures, options and swaps to manage risk.
notes: Hedge ratio for minimum variance: h = ρ σS ÷ σF.
Options give the right, not the obligation; premiums are the cost of protection.
Interest rate swaps change fixed to floating exposure or vice versa.

topics.title: Restructuring and insolvency
topics.summary: Buybacks, demergers and the IBC.
notes: Buyback limit: 25% of paid-up capital and free reserves (with debt–equity not above 2:1 after buyback).
Demergers separate business units into new companies.
IBC: corporate insolvency resolution within 180 days (extendable to 330 days including litigation).

courses.title: Indirect Taxes: GST and Customs, MCom Semester 4
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (BU MCom CBCS, 2025-26)

topics.title: Constitutional and legal framework
topics.summary: GST laws, the GST Council and dual structure.
notes: Laws: CGST Act, SGST Acts, IGST Act, UTGST Act, GST (Compensation to States) Act.
Article 246A gives both Centre and States power to levy GST.
Inter-state supplies attract IGST, settled between Centre and States.
outcomes: Explain the legal framework of GST
Classify supplies for CGST, SGST or IGST

topics.title: Value of supply and input tax credit
topics.summary: Transaction value, inclusions and ITC rules.
notes: Value of supply is the transaction value plus taxes other than GST, incidental expenses and subsidies linked to price (section 15).
Discounts before or at supply recorded on the invoice are excluded.
ITC is reversed if payment to the supplier is not made within 180 days.

topics.title: Registration, invoicing, returns and e-invoicing
topics.summary: Compliance under GST.
notes: E-invoicing applies above a turnover threshold (₹5 crore).
Reverse charge applies to notified supplies (e.g. GTA, legal services to businesses).
Annual return GSTR-9; reconciliation statement GSTR-9C for larger taxpayers.

topics.title: Customs law
topics.summary: Types of customs duty and valuation of imports.
notes: Basic customs duty, IGST on imports, social welfare surcharge, safeguard and anti-dumping duties.
Assessable value = CIF value (transaction value + freight + insurance).
Baggage, warehousing and drawback provisions.
outcomes: Compute customs duty on an import
